<thought>To determine the number of methyl (CH₃) groups in the unknown sample, the most direct approach is to obtain its ¹³C NMR spectrum (no arguments needed). Methyl carbons typically appear in the 10–30 ppm region. By counting the distinct peaks in that region we can infer the number of methyl carbon environments, which corresponds to the number of methyl groups present (assuming none are symmetry‑equivalent). This requires only a single, inexpensive measurement.</thought>
